paper_ratings.evidence_note: UEGAN supports unpaired GAN-based aesthetic enhancement and content fidelity, but does not specifically study low-light realism or the named lighting attributes.
GPP-LLIE directly studies perceptually realistic low-light enhancement, but uses VLM-guided diffusion rather than an unpaired GAN or demonstrated user-preference alignment.
The paper addresses dynamic video content and memorability, but not emotional narration, educational videos, or narrated-versus-nonnarrated comparisons.
QAGAN learns user-supplied quality characteristics from unpaired images using attention, but its abstract does not establish low-light-specific perceptual realism.
The abstract concerns dynamic video memorability rather than image enhancement, attention, perceptual priors, or unpaired training.
The paper describes a video memorability benchmark, not image enhancement or its proposed mechanisms.
Multimodal video memorability prediction does not ground the proposed image enhancement framework.
QAGAN explicitly provides unpaired image enhancement with quality attention and user-provided high-quality image characteristics, grounding a central proposed component.

The method explicitly combines audio gestalt with visual and semantic features to predict video memorability, directly grounding the proposed feature integration; the abstract does not quantify an ablation improvement.
The task overview describes memorability prediction on action-rich videos, but reports no test of emotional narration or educational video comparisons.
The paper addresses video memorability prediction and dataset challenges but does not examine audio gestalt or audio-feature fusion.
Unsupervised image enhancement with GANs does not address audio, video memorability, or multimodal prediction.
Low-light image enhancement with perceptual priors provides no evidence about video memorability prediction.
Quality-attention image enhancement does not address audio gestalt or video memorability prediction.
GPP-LLIE explicitly develops global and local generative perceptual priors for low-light enhancement, grounding the perceptual-prior component, though it does not validate the proposed integration.
The benchmark covers short- and long-term video memorability, but not audio gestalt fusion or its incremental benefit.
Audio gestalt is considered as a predictor of video memorability, but narration emotion and educational-versus-action-rich comparisons are not examined.
UEGAN directly addresses unpaired aesthetic image enhancement and uses feature-domain fidelity loss to preserve content, grounding key framework requirements.

association_checks.evidence_note: The collection studies video memorability, and the audio-gestalt paper explicitly fuses auditory, visual, and semantic features. It grounds the premise, although a short-term-only improvement over a no-audio baseline is not demonstrated in the abstracts.
All three papers concern video memorability and some discuss action-rich content or audio features, but none tests emotional narration in educational videos against non-narrated action-rich videos.
The collection concerns video memorability, not unpaired image enhancement, quality attention, or generative perceptual priors.

QAGAN supplies unpaired quality attention, GPP-LLIE supplies perceptual priors, and UEGAN supplies unpaired enhancement with content fidelity. These substantively motivate the proposed combination, but do not demonstrate its robustness or integration.
The papers concern still-image enhancement, not audio gestalt, video memorability, or fusion of audio with visual and semantic cues.

The collection combines evidence for unpaired GAN enhancement and user-specified aesthetics (QAGAN/UEGAN) with perceptually realistic low-light enhancement (GPP-LLIE). No paper establishes the full combined GAN-based low-light method.
